title: Install Failure Heuristics - Field Guide
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic field guide for first-pass triage and minimal smoke probes when private deployments (VPC or on-prem) fail during install or early runtime after an upgrade. It's intentionally a heuristics notebook — quick checks, reproducible probes, and concrete commands to narrow down root cause fast.

Scope & audience:
- Engineers: solutions, SRE, release engineering who are first responders for customer private deployments.
- Covers: bootstrap/install failures, TF module mismatch, early runtime crashes, GPU/kernel-level OOMs, kv-cache warm failure, and network-sensitive VPC failures.
- Not a full runbook: use alongside onprem-first-responder-checklist and TF rollback playbooks.

Quick mental model (5 min):
- Verify: cluster nodes are "up" at infra level (cloud/metal) -> kernel/hw errors -> kube/node agent -> docker/runtime -> redwood runtime -> model load -> inference path.
- Always correlate: TF state vs live resources vs operator config. Mismatches are frequent after partial upgrades.

First-response checklist (10–20 min):
1) Confirm customer impact and symptoms: install hang / pod CrashLoop / slow startup / degraded throughput / 503s.
2) Grab high-level status: kubectl get nodes,pods -A; terraform state list (if customer provides); systemd status on hosts.
3) Capture logs (persist): agent logs, bootstrap logs, kubelet, system journal, dmesg, nvme/nvlink logs. Save into /tmp/triage-<timestamp>.tgz.

Minimal smoke probe sequence (order matters):
A. Control-plane sanity (2–3 commands)
- kubectl get pods -n redwood --show-labels 
- kubectl describe pod <bootstrap-pod> | grep -i -E "Error|Failed|OOM|Image"
- check certs: openssl s_client -connect <controlplane-host>:443 -servername <host> (if TLS handshake failing)

B. Node/driver health
- ssh into one affected node
- sudo dmesg | tail -n 200  # look for kernel OOM, GPU driver resets, firmware failure
- nvidia-smi -q || sudo cat /var/log/nvidia-installer.log
- check iommu/NUMA messages and BMC reachability

C. TF module and resource parity (critical after upgrades)
- terraform show -json > tf-live.json  (run from infra account/supplied state)
- local sanity: check that count(module.gpu_pool.*) in state matches expected in workspace vars
- Quick heuristics: if tf-state reports 0 GPU nodes but k8s shows node objects -> likely drift or failed ASG attach

D. Runtime startup & model load
- tail -n +1 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | sed -n '1,200p'  # look for model unpack errors, kernel selection warnings
- common fingerprint: "failed to mmap weights" -> usually permission or disk corruption
- common fingerprint: "incompatible kernel for quantized ops" -> kernel mismatch or missing libs

Failure fingerprints and quick mitigations (fast wins):
- "ImagePullBackOff" + "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" -> image registry certs or private ECR auth; check node /etc/docker/certs.d and imagePullSecrets in pod spec.
- "failed to mmap" or "bad magic" -> weight file corrupted during transfer; re-pull model artifacts (aws s3 sync or scp) and verify sha256.
- "driver timeout/kernel panic" -> GPU firmware mismatch; check driver version matrix in infra-notes and try node reboot out-of-band.
- "bootstrap task hung at CHECK_CONFIG" -> TF variables mismatch (look for missing env var or secret); re-run bootstrap with --dry-run flag if available.
- "OOM when allocating KV cache" -> model sharding vs node memory mismatch; reduce kv cache in runtime config or scale to larger instance.

Terraform module notes (practical heuristics):
- Frequently changed vars: gpu_instance_type, ami_id, node_labels.template, kubelet_extra_args. When upgrading modules, ensure the new module uses the same tag names for node pools; otherwise taints/labels break auto-detection.
- Use `terraform state list | grep module.gpu` to find expected resources. If resources exist in cloud but not in state, suspect manual drift.
- When module changes rename resources (lifecycle -> create_before_destroy missing), the operator may see duplicate node names leading to install failure. Consider `terraform state mv` fixes or roll forward with careful orchestrated drain.
- Note about provider versions: provider aws v4.x vs v5.x changed default encryption settings for EBS; after upgrade mounts may fail with mount helper errors. Check terraform providers.tf pinned versions in customer repo.

Upgrade plan preflight (5 checks before apply):
- Confirm node image (AMI/container) hashes match release matrix file.
- Smoke deploy to a single canary node: taint secondaries and run module changes only against one instance.
- Run `make test-smoke` (internal) which executes model-load + tiny inference vectors. Collect token latency and memory trace.
- Snapshot / create backups of TF state and etcd before applying (mandatory for on-prem).
- Have a rollback plan: automated TF rollback script and known-good artifacts accessible offline.

Repro tips (when customer can't share full access):
- Ask for:
  - systemd/journal logs around failure time
  - kube describe + pod logs
  - terraform state snapshot (obfuscated if necessary)
  - small tar of /var/log/redwood and /etc/redwood (config)
- Provide a tiny diagnostic script to run that collects the above and uploads to our secure triage bucket.

Sample commands we repeatedly use in field (copy-paste friendly):
- kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide
- kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> --previous
- ssh root@<node> 'sudo journalctl -u redwood-bootstrap -n 500' > bootstrap.log
- ssh root@<node> 'sudo dmesg | tail -n 200' > dmesg.log
- aws s3api head-object --bucket <artifact-bkt> --key models/<model>/weights.tar.gz --query Checksum

Escalation & who to loop in (fast path):
- If kernel/GPU driver issues -> eng-infra (ops) + serving-runtime on-call (pager)
- If TF-state drift or provider bug suspected -> platform-engineering + release-eng
- If model artifact corruption or signing problem -> applied-ml + infra-SRE for bucket ACLs

Post-incident prompts (for a short postmortem):
- What changed in the upgrade? list terraform module diffs and image hashes.
- Was TF state mutated manually? who did it and why?
- Did we have automation to detect node-label drift? If not, add a 5-min reconciler alert.
- Action items (owner, ETA, test plan).

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- Add a small python diagnostic that validates kernel/libc/driver compatibility matrix and uploads a compact report. (Ravi)
- Integrate preflight model-load into terraform as a post-create hook for canary nodes (proposal). (Elena)
- Create a standard sha256-based model artifact verification step in bootstrap. (Derek)

Notes-to-self / heuristics baggage: 
- If you see a sequence of "Backoff" -> often a permission or secret issue, not a runtime code bug.
- Always capture /var/log/redwood with timestamps; customers often truncate logs which loses root cause.
- When running remote diagnostics, prefer `--previous` logs to catch crashes during init.

Appendix: quick map of common error strings -> likely root cause
- "ImagePullBackOff" + "x509" -> registry certs / pull secret
- "failed to mmap" -> disk / permission / corrupted artifact
- "cuda: invalid device function" -> mismatched CUDA vs binary build
- "kubelet: failing to start container" + "mount: unknown fs type" -> missing kernel module or EBS mount helper mismatch

End of guide.
This is intentionally concise — feedback welcome. If you make field changes, add a single-line changelog at top next edit.
